research.claim: Pizzeria Sei in Palms serves Tokyo-influenced Neapolitan pizza; its margherita has blistered edges, tomato sauce, and buffalo mozzarella.
Pizzeria Sei tied for second place in the 2026 50 Top Pizza U.S. ranking.
At Pizzeria Sei, the Bismarck pizza is topped with prosciutto cotto, egg, fior di latte, pecorino, basil, truffle oil, and sea salt.
Dtown Pizzeria in West Hollywood makes Detroit-style pies with sauce on top and crusty corners; its menu includes a classic pepperoni version.
Quarter Sheets in Echo Park serves thick-crust pan pizzas, Sicilian squares, and tomato slices; one listed pie is the Red Top, with mozzarella, red sauce, grana, and basil.

Bub & Grandma’s Pizza at 5101 York Boulevard in Highland Park is a takeout-only East Coast-style sourdough slice shop; its Potato White pie has potato, caramelized onion, Taleggio, mozzarella, Parmesan, and fried rosemary.

Pizzana’s Diavola is topped with spicy salami and nduja-walnut romesco, and the restaurant has Los Angeles locations including Brentwood, Marina del Rey, Sherman Oaks, West Hollywood, and Silver Lake.
Prime Pizza serves New York-style pizza by the slice and as 18-inch pies, and also offers square, vegan, and gluten-free options.

output.body:
Number 5: Detroit-style crusty corners make Dtown Pizzeria’s classic pepperoni my crunch pick. The sauce goes on top, so order that.

Number 4: Quarter Sheets’ thick-crust Red Top is the cheesier, softer pan-pie pick. Order it with mozzarella, red sauce, grana, and basil.

Number 3: When you want heat, Pizzana’s Diavola brings spicy salami and nduja-walnut romesco. That nutty, savory combo beats a standard spicy pie; order it.

Number 2: Bub & Grandma’s is takeout-only, so this is the pie to bring home. The Potato White pairs potato and caramelized onion with Taleggio, mozzarella, Parmesan, and fried rosemary.

Number 1: I’ll admit, egg on pizza sounds odd. But the Bismarck wins for its prosciutto cotto and egg, finished with truffle oil. At Pizzeria Sei, order it with fior di latte, pecorino, basil, and sea salt; that combination makes it the most memorable order here.
